sections.content: How many people stayed in Colchester after gaining qualifications?

Colchester is a large town in the East of England. Colchester also has a university.

Colchester has medium levels of deprivation.

Overall, Colchester ended up with:

  • a similar number of graduates as it produced
  • more non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 5,330 state-school pupils from Colchester who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 1,655 (31%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 1,535 (29%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Colchester to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Colchester's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Colchester in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Colchester move to?

Of Colchester's graduates, 650 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 50 of those graduates (8%) were living fairly locally, in the Colchester travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Colchester's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 335 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 85 of those qualified non-graduates (25%) were living fairly locally, in the Colchester travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Colchester's GCSE cohort:

  • 445 graduates left the East of England
  • the most common region they moved to was London
  • 130 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the East of England
  • the most common region they moved to was London

In 2018 to 2019, 45% of graduates and 39% of qualified non-graduates living in Colchester had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 1,775 graduates and 1,920 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Colchester. This is compared with the 1,655 graduates and 1,535 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 55% of the graduates had also lived in Colchester as GCSE pupils, while 45% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Colchester in 2018 to 2019, 61% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 39% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
